en.title: Netflix's The Age of Innocence Arrives February 2027 With Stunning First Look
en.summary: Get ready to journey back to 19th-century New York. Netflix has officially unveiled the release date and a series of captivating first-look images for its ambitious adaptation of Edith Wharton's classic novel, The Age of Innocence.
en.body:
Netflix is dialing up the drama with its upcoming 8-episode series, **The Age of Innocence**, set to debut on February 28, 2027. This lavish period piece, adapted from **Edith Wharton**'s seminal 1920 novel, promises to immerse viewers in the opulent yet restrictive world of New York's Gilded Age elite.

Leading the charge is showrunner **Emma Frost**, a name synonymous with high-quality historical dramas, having previously helmed **The White Queen**, **The White Princess**, and **The Spanish Princess**. Her expertise in navigating intricate historical settings and compelling character arcs is precisely what fans will hope for as she tackles Wharton's poignant story of forbidden love and societal obligation. The series stars **Camila Morrone**, known for **Something Very Bad is Going to Happen**, alongside **Kristine Froseth** (**The Buccaneers**) and **Ben Radcliffe** (**The Witcher**), hinting at a dynamic central trio.

## A Glimpse into Gilded Age Society

The first-look images offer a tantalizing peek into the meticulous production design and costume work. We see **Kristine Froseth** as May Welland and **Ben Radcliffe** as Newland Archer, captured in moments that suggest the simmering tensions and unspoken emotions characteristic of the novel. Filming for the series took place primarily in Prague, Czech Republic, from September 2025 to February 2026, indicating a significant investment in bringing this classic story to life with authenticity and visual splendor. The narrative centers on a complex love triangle, a hallmark of Wharton's work, exploring the suffocating expectations of New York society and the personal sacrifices made in its name. This adaptation has been in development for some time, and the release of these images marks a significant milestone in its journey to the screen.

## The Enduring Appeal of Wharton's Masterpiece

**The Age of Innocence** is no stranger to adaptation, having captivated audiences on stage and screen for decades. Its previous iteration as a beloved 1993 film directed by **Martin Scorsese**, starring **Daniel Day-Lewis**, **Michelle Pfeiffer**, and **Winona Ryder**, set a high bar. This new Netflix series faces the challenge of not only honoring the source material but also bringing a fresh perspective to a story that continues to resonate with modern audiences. The appeal lies in its exploration of universal themes: the conflict between personal desire and social duty, the consequences of choices made under pressure, and the quiet heartbreak of missed opportunities. Fans are eager to see how **Emma Frost** and her cast will interpret these timeless elements for a new generation of binge-watchers.

## What's Next

With a confirmed release date of February 28, 2027, and production already wrapped, the focus now shifts to the marketing campaign leading up to the premiere. Viewers can anticipate further trailers and interviews as Netflix builds anticipation for this major period drama.

We also have a ton of new first-look images to check out as well.  The Age of Innocence is heading to Netflix on February 28, 2027 . The series comes from showrunner Emma Frost, who is best known for her period dramas The White Queen, The White Princess , and The Spanish Princess . The 8-episode series is an adaptation of the classic 1920 novel of the same name by Edith Wharton, described as a passionate and heart-rending ‘will-they/won’t-they’ love triangle set in 19th-century New York. The series is headlined by Netflix’s Something Very Bad is Going to Happen star Camila Morrone alongside Kristine Froseth ( The Buccaneers ) and Ben Radcliffe, whom Netflix viewers may recognise from his role as Giselher in The Witcher .  Also involved on the series as executive producers are Peter Chernin, Jenno Topping, Tracey Cook (Chernin Entertainment) and Pavlina Hatoupis. Netflix’s adaptation of The Age of Innocence has been in the works for quite some time. The series began filming in September 2025, shooting mainly in Prague, Czech Republic. It wrapped filming in February 2026. The novel has been adapted several times before across different mediums. It was a successful Broadway Play from Margaret Ayer Barnes back in 1928. It was later adapted into a requisite movie in 1993, directed by Martin Scorsese and starring Daniel Day-Lewis, Michelle Pfeiffer, and Winona Ryder. “I was at a place where I said I want to do anything except period, because I’ve done so much period,” Frost told Vanity Fair , noting that Netflix’s offer to adapt the novel was an opportunity too tempting to pass up. “I remembered it was the very first love story I ever engaged with that felt truly adult.” What is The Age of Innocence about? The Age of Innocence follows Newland Archer, a wealthy, well-educated gentleman lawyer who is smitten by Ellen Olenska, who has recently returned to New York high society after fleeing her marriage to a wealthy Polish count. “The story is about the choice between following your heart or staying with duty and convention,” showrunner Emma Frost told Netflix.  Check out the official logline down below: Based on Edith Wharton’s classic novel of forbidden love in 19th century New York, The Age Of Innocence is a passionate and heart-rending will-they/won’t-they love triangle exploring themes of freedom, duty, identity and love in all its forms. This fresh take is true to Wharton’s novel but will speak to a new generation as we traverse the ballrooms and bedrooms of these young people, asking the question what is love — and what is lust?
